newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni soldiers killed in tourist hostage siege.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni soldiers killed in tourist hostage siege.

text.p: Yemeni tribesmen holding European tourists hostage fired rocket-propelled grenades at surrounding military forces, killing three soldiers and wounding five, witnesses said on Saturday.

In the second kidnapping involving European holidaymakers this month, members of the Al al-Masni tribe abducted five tourists this week in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.

"Some of the tribesmen attacked the security forces which were surrounding the area in dozens of military trucks," a witness told Reuters. "They attacked the forces with RPGs, killing three and injuring five."
Diplomats said the attack, which occurred late on Friday, also injured a number of villagers, but they said tribal sources had confirmed the hostages were unharmed.

Initial reports said there were only four hostages, all of whom were said to be Dutch. But diplomats said latest information indicated three men and two women had been abducted, and it was not clear whether they were Dutch or Polish.
Security officials in the capital Sanaa would neither confirm nor deny the shooting incident.
But an official told Reuters that negotiations with the kidnappers were continuing with the help of other tribes who were mediating between the government and the kidnappers.
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were abducted and briefly held by tribesmen while touring an area 240 km (150 miles) north of Sanaa.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or other foreigners as bargaining chips.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.

This week's kidnapping was the first involving the Al al-Masni tribe, which lives in the Beni Jabr area near Khawlan. There were conflicting reports of when the tourists had been seized but diplomats said they appeared to have been abducted between Tuesday and Thursday.
